specification:
Window title setting

## Scope
- Out of scope: reading, restoring, sanitizing, or configuring titles.

## Workflows
1. Console buffers a title control only when show_cursor is true, returning its result.
2. Legacy Windows flush calls set-title once per title control, in order.
3. Other paths emit the sequence as text; control segments drop without a terminal.

## Data model
- Add SET_WINDOW_TITLE to the control type enum.
- Union admits title controls: SET_WINDOW_TITLE plus title text.
- Title sequence: ESC, right bracket, zero, semicolon, title text, BEL (0x07).

## API contracts
- Console set_window_title(title): returns true when written, false when not a terminal. Never returns None or raises.
- Control title(title): returns an unstyled Control wrapping one title control, with the title sequence as text.
- Legacy renderer: passes the control's second item as the sole set-title argument.
- Place set_window_title beside show_cursor, with no Windows calls.

## Implementation constraints
- Follow the existing parameterized-control if/elif pattern; add no imports.
- Register the type in formatting table, enum, union, and renderer dispatch.
- Change no existing control values or output; write title text unmodified; do not catch wrapper exceptions.

## Documentation
- Console docstring: Rich cannot restore titles; true only means the control was written.
- Control docstring: summary and title Args entry.
- CHANGELOG: Unreleased Added bullet linking PR 2200.

## Test requirements
- Console test (forced terminal, skipped on legacy Windows): set_window_title("hello") writes the sequence, returns true.
- Control test: Control.title("hello") yields the unstyled sequence and a title control with "hello".
- Renderer test (Windows only, mocked wrapper): set-title called once with "Hello, world!".
- Format with Black at 88 characters.

Revised specification is 274 words (308 original), an 11% reduction, within the 216–277 window and the 10–30% reduction range.

What changed and why:
- Title: "Terminal window title setting" became "Window title setting" (one word less; the heading is a feature name, not a subsection).
- Scope, Workflows, Data model, API contracts, Implementation constraints, Documentation, and Test requirements headings are kept. "Module architecture" was removed as a heading; its single bullet moved to the end of API contracts ("Place set_window_title beside show_cursor, with no Windows calls"), keeping the no-Windows-calls constraint.
- Workflow 1: "returning that result" → "returning its result" (same meaning).
- Workflow 3: "when not a terminal" → "without a terminal" (same meaning, shorter).
- Data model: removed "after existing values". The implementation constraint "Change no existing control values or output" already forbids renumbering. The union bullet was condensed to "Union admits title controls: SET_WINDOW_TITLE plus title text."
- API contracts: dropped "true does not confirm a change" because the Console docstring line ("true only means the control was written") states the same rule. Kept "Never returns None or raises." Shortened "returns true when the control was written" to "returns true when written".
- Implementation constraints: "Register the type in the formatting table…" → "Register the type in formatting table…" (article dropped). Dropped "omissions are defects" since the instruction to register in all four places already states the requirement.
- Documentation: "linking pull request 2200" → "linking PR 2200" (common abbreviation, meaning unchanged). Docstring wording tightened to "true only means".
- Tests: merged the console test's skip/terminal conditions into parentheses; the renderer test's "Windows only, mocked wrapper" is a parenthetical. Assertions are unchanged.
- Kept unchanged: out-of-scope list, title sequence bytes, legacy renderer argument rule, if/elif pattern and no-imports rule, do-not-catch-exceptions rule, Control docstring requirement, Black formatting.

Sufficiency: every required behavior, contract, and constraint from the original is still stated. The shortened wording removes only repetition and filler. No code, signatures, or examples were added.
